summary: The executor timed out after 2100s (executor_timed_out) before completing the PostgreSQL TLS replication setup. Package installation, CA distribution, and TLS certificate/config staging succeeded on all three nodes, but the last observed pg_hba.conf on node1 still only had the default scram-sha-256 rules with no TLS/client-certificate enforcement for replication, and no evidence of pg_hba edits, service restarts, or standby bootstrapping (pg_basebackup, standby.signal, primary_conninfo) appears in the selected record set before the timeout.

evidence.source: executor command audit, node1/node2/node3 apt-get install commands
evidence.finding: Each apt-get install call exceeded the platform's 120s proxy read timeout and was reported as 'failed', even though the install had actually completed on the host (node1's dpkg -l shows postgresql-16 fully installed with post-bootstrap init messages).

evidence.source: executor command audit, node2/node3 polling commands
evidence.finding: After the apt 'failure', the executor had to run explicit 100s polling loops on node2 and node3 to wait for the background apt-get process to finish, adding further wall-clock time before it could confirm postgresql-16 was installed.

evidence.source: executor command audit, CA/cert distribution steps
evidence.finding: A CA tarball (pgca.tgz) was built and served via a temporary HTTP server, downloaded successfully by node2 and node3, and TLS material (ca.crt, server.crt/key, replicator.crt/key) was copied into /etc/postgresql/16/main/tls on all three nodes with correct ownership/permissions.
An identical conf.d/tls_repl.conf enabling ssl, ssl_cert_file/ssl_key_file/ssl_ca_file, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, and hot_standby was written on all three nodes.

evidence.source: executor command audit, last pg_hba.conf check on node1
evidence.finding: pg_hba.conf on node1 at the time of this check still contained only the default local/peer and scram-sha-256 rules (including for the 'replication' database) — no hostssl rule requiring a client certificate from the new CA had been added yet.

44 of 62 terminal command records were omitted from the redacted set (only up to 20 failures + 12 successes retained), so it cannot be confirmed with certainty that no further progress happened after the last shown pg_hba.conf check; absence of later evidence is not proof of no later action.

likely_causes.cause: Cumulative time lost to the apt-get install step (three sequential ~125s proxy-timeout 'failures' plus two 100s polling waits, roughly 8-9 minutes total) consumed a disproportionate share of the 35-minute execution budget before any TLS/replication configuration began.
Per-node sequential execution (running the same install/config command three times, once per node, rather than in parallel) multiplied the time cost of every slow step across the whole session.

The task was not finished when the timeout hit: pg_hba.conf had not yet been updated to require TLS + client certificates from the new CA for replication connections, and no evidence of PostgreSQL restart, standby pg_basebackup, or primary_conninfo/standby.signal configuration was present in the visible records, suggesting the executor ran out of time before reaching the replication-bootstrap phase.

The apt-get 'failed' outcome was a proxy/tool artifact (120s Proxy Read Timeout) rather than an actual package-manager failure, but the executor may have spent additional turns investigating/retrying under the mistaken belief that the install itself had failed.

next_attempt_guidance: Run apt-get install in the background with output redirected to a log file and a PID file, then poll with short exec calls, instead of a single foreground call — this avoids hitting the platform's 120s proxy read timeout on all three nodes and prevents wasted retries/investigation.

Where nodes have no dependency on each other (e.g. installing postgresql, copying the CA bundle, writing conf.d/tls_repl.conf), issue the exec calls for node1/node2/node3 back-to-back without waiting on each one sequentially, to reduce total wall-clock time within the fixed session budget.

After TLS material and conf.d changes are in place, immediately add explicit hostssl pg_hba.conf rules for the replication database requiring clientcert=verify-full tied to the new CA (e.g. `hostssl replication replicator 0.0.0.0/0 cert clientcert=verify-full`) before moving on — do this early rather than leaving it for a later pass, since it is central to the task requirement of accepting replication only from CA-issued certs.

Verify actual package/service state with idempotent checks (e.g. `dpkg -l | grep postgresql-16`, `systemctl is-active postgresql`) rather than trusting a tool-reported timeout as a functional failure, to avoid unnecessary re-work.

Reserve time explicitly for the replica bootstrap phase (pg_basebackup from node1, standby.signal or primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and sslcert/sslkey pointing at the replicator certificate, postgresql restart) since this phase had not started by the time of the last observed evidence — consider doing a time-budget check partway through the session and prioritizing this phase if time is short.

Do not assume the old cluster's partial state is reusable; start fresh and re-run the full sequence (CA creation, cert distribution, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf edits, restart, replica bootstrap, verification with `SELECT * FROM pg_stat_replication` on node1) end-to-end on the new cluster.
